packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 15 - unverified image reading

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this item. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..016 of this packet (I listed the image filenames in the packet directory; packet.json was not read). I viewed the images as supplied; no web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

IMAGE MAP
- Strip A, face 1: image-001 overview; image-002 (left half), image-003 (right half).
- Strip A, face 2: image-004 overview; image-005 (left half), image-006 (right half).
- Strip B, face 1: image-007 overview; image-008 (left half), image-009 (right half).
- Strip B, face 2: image-010 overview; image-011 (left half), image-012 (right half).
- Scrap C, face 1: image-013 overview with ruler; image-014 the same face cropped (not a different area).
- Scrap C, face 2: image-015 overview with ruler; image-016 the same face cropped.
The two halves of each strip face overlap in the middle. That A, B and C are three separate pieces is my inference from their different outlines; that they come from one leaf is not established, though hand and rubrication look alike.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation unless marked)
- Strip A and strip B are each about 7.5 cm wide by 2 cm high; scrap C about 5 cm by 2-2.5 cm, with an irregular torn upper edge and holes. Strip A has a large irregular hole and a deep notch; strip B has a rectangular notch cut from the lower edge about 2 cm from one end.
- On each strip a vertical fold with a narrow overlap or seam divides a short end section (about 2 cm) from the longer section. The short end section carries dark, well-preserved ink; the longer section is rubbed and stained and much fainter. The long section of strip A face 1 has brown adhesive or leather stain along the fold.
- Text is horizontal and upright as displayed on all faces. Five to six lines per strip face, the top and bottom lines cut through. Line spacing about 4 mm.
- Tentative interpretation: the fold may be the gutter of a small bifolium, so the short end section and the long section would belong to two different pages rather than one continuous line. Alternatively it is a single page with a pasted repair. I transcribe the two sections separately and do not join words across the fold.
- Script: a formal gothic book hand (textualis/hybrida type), black-brown ink. The language is a Germanic vernacular, not Latin (word forms such as "dinghe", "leuen", "woerden", "sprekende", "van", "ende"); the rubric on strip B face 1 is in Latin or a Latin-looking form.
- Rubrication: red paraph signs (strip A face 2 lower left; strip B face 1, two; scrap C face 1 lower left); a red rubric of two words on strip B face 1; red strokes touching capitals (strip B face 2, scrap C face 2); a red letter like "T" or a paraph with a short red stroke at the top of strip A face 1; red letters at the lower right of scrap C face 1.
- No running title, no enlarged initial, no gloss visible. Columns cannot be judged from strips this narrow.

SELECTION
All faces attempted. The short end sections of strips A and B are legible; the long sections and scrap C are only partly legible. No span reaches ten lines because no face has more than six.

TRANSCRIPTION

Strip A, face 1 - short end section (left), image-002 (also at the left of image-001)
image-002 line 1: [...]ers(?) doen m[...]   (first letters damaged; "ee"/"er" before long s; possibly one word "[...]ersdoen")
image-002 line 2: [...]in(?) gh[...] [surface abraded, illegible]
image-002 line 3: [...]im(?)/uu(?) ae[...] [abraded]
image-002 line 4: [...]r(?)doen(?) [abraded] [...]
image-002 line 5 (lower half cut): [illegible] ...h(?)e... [illegible]

Strip A, face 1 - long section (right), image-002 right part and image-003
image-002 line 1: [red sign: a "T"-shaped letter or paraph, followed by a short red stroke] [illegible]
image-003 line 1: [...] [hole] [...]n(?) e(?) c(?)... dev(?)/den(?)[...]
image-003 line 2: [illegible] ...sch(?)... [illegible]

image-003 line 4: [illegible] [hole] [illegible]
image-003 line 5: [illegible] ...oe(?)...
(This side of the long section is too faint to give words.)

Strip A, face 2 - long section (left), image-005 and left part of image-006
image-005 line 1 (upper half cut): [...] van(?) [...] | image-006: ...ue(?)/uc(?) ...
image-005 line 2: [illegible, about two words, ? ending "-de"] [notch] | image-006: [...] ...ede(?)...
image-005 line 3: [illegible] ...t(?) h(?)ae(?)... [hole] [...]m(?) alle(?) ... | image-006: ... wille(?)/wil m(?)...
image-005 line 4: ...w(?)... [hole] | image-006: ...M(?)... [illegible]

image-006 line 1 (cut, descenders only): [illegible]
image-006 line 2: [...]ene(?) in tafel(?)   (last word "tafel"/"tasel"; the final letter is at the cut edge)
image-006 line 3: [...]n dinghe m[...]   ("dinghe" has a hooked abbreviation or flourish over the final e, possibly "dinghen")
image-006 line 4: [...]s(?)t(?)elike leue(n)   (the letters before "-elike" lie in the fold: "gh"/"st"; a mark over the final "e" of "leue" is uncertain)
image-006 line 5: [...]heit vlace(?)   ("vlace"/"vlact"/"place"; the first letter of the second word is v-shaped)

(Faint; none of these is secure.)

image-009 line 2 (RUBRIC, red ink): Prima(?) siti(?)[superscript mark: -s / -o ?] [red point]   (first word could also be "Pruna"/"Pruina"/"Prime"; the minims are not separable. Second word begins with long s, then "iti"/"cti", ending in a raised loop.) Before the rubric, in black: co(?)/eo(?)
image-009 line 3: D(?)[...] e(n)d(e)(?)/ed'(?) co(?)e6(?)/coes(?) vn(?)/un(?)[...]   (large first letter at the notch edge, "D" or "R"; middle abraded)

image-009 line 5 (lower part cut): [...]h(?)e(?)[...]sc(?)hon(?)/rsoen(?) n(?)[...]

image-011 line 1 (upper part cut): [...] ...ene(?)/eine(?) [red-touched letter, ? "a"/"d"] ...
image-011 line 2: [...]a(?)[...] [red vertical stroke] Da(?)[...] [abraded] ...
image-011 line 3: [...]lle(?) ghesel(?)[...]   (possibly "alle ghesel..."; the letters after "ghesel" are rubbed: "sc"/"le")

image-012 line 1: [...]ne(?) bekenne(?)/beghinne(?) elcke(?)/clocke(?) ende(?)/onder(?) ...elic(?)
image-012 line 2: [...] ghe(?)... die(?)/mec(?) en(de)(?) neghe(?)/negh'n(?) ...   (a word "eñ" with abbreviation stroke is fairly clear)

image-012 line 4: [...] ...sen(?) ... oec(?)/oir(?) ... ende(?)/ondelic(?) ...
image-012 line 5 (tops only): [illegible]

Scrap C, face 1 (image-013 and its crop image-014; one face, counted from the top of image-014)
image-014 line 1 (fragmentary, by the holes): [...]n(?)... [hole] ... ste(?)...
image-014 line 2: [...] ...ro(?)u(?)... [hole] ... ghe(?)/gh'(?) ...
image-014 line 3: [...]hui(?)s(?) a(?) ...ende(?) ...   (very rubbed)
image-014 line 4: [...] ...he(?) ... ...man(?)/nam(?) [...]
image-014 line 5: [red paraph] [red point] [notch] [illegible] [RED letters:] S(?)c(?)a(?) [...] [red strokes]   (a red word of four or five letters beginning with a large round letter, "S"/"G"; possibly a rubric or a nomen-sacrum form; not secure)

Scrap C, face 2 (image-015 and its crop image-016; counted from the top of image-016)
image-016 line 1 (upper part cut): [...]n(?) hi(?)s(?)/bis(?) [hole] ...
image-016 line 2: [...] ...n(?) die(?) es(?) [hole] le(?)[...]
image-016 line 3: [...] ...ene(?)n woerde(n)   (the last word is clear as "woerde" with an abbreviation stroke over the final e; before it perhaps "sine(n)"/"dine(n)"/"enen")
image-016 line 4: [...] ...m(?)et(?) ... elck(?)/elic(?) hae(r)(?)/baer(?)
image-016 line 5: [red stroke on a capital, ? "D"/"E"] [...] sprekende(?)   (the ending "-ekende"/"-ckende" is clear; "spr" before it is rubbed)
image-016 line 6: [...] ...n(?) en(?) ghe(?)[notch]...oi(?)/ou(?)
Left edge strip of scrap C face 2 (a folded-over sliver, separate from the lines above; only line beginnings/endings):
image-016, beside line 3: ...en(?) ; beside line 4: [large letter, ? "E"/"C"]s(?) ; beside line 5: G(?)e(?)/E(?)[...] ; beside line 6: m(?)e(?)/nie(?)

MOST USABLE ANCHORS (still to be treated as uncertain)
- Strip A face 2, short section: "... in tafel(?) / ...n dinghe m... / ...elike leue(n) / ...heit vlace(?)".
- Strip B face 1, short section: red rubric of two words, "Prima(?) siti(?)...", followed by lines containing "van p(er)so...".
- Strip B face 2: "...lle ghesel(?)...".
- Scrap C face 2: "... woerde(n) / ... / ... sprekende".

LIMITATIONS
- Every line is truncated at both ends by the cut of the strip, and the top and bottom lines of each face are sliced through, so no complete sentence exists.
- The long sections of both strips are abraded and stained; readings there are letter-shape guesses.
- The relationship of the short end section to the long section (same page or conjoint leaf) is unknown, as is the order of strips A, B and C and which face is recto.
- u/n/m/i minims are frequently indistinguishable at this state of preservation; where I give two alternatives I could not decide.
- The language is a Germanic vernacular on the evidence of the word forms; I have not tried to determine dialect and have not normalised spellings.
- A wider view does not exist for these pieces; raking light or UV on the long sections would be the useful next step.
